_note: D3 is the FALLBACK, not the default. Use it ONLY for chart types Vega-Lite cannot express — sankey, treemap, chord, sunburst, force-network (all tagged vega_lite_native:false in chart_chooser.json). For everything else build a Vega-Lite spec (vega_recipes.json). D3 is an allowed CDN (component_implementations.json). These are recipe OUTLINES — D3 module + layout generator + the data shape — not full code. Inline the data; one self-contained index.html on file://.
_sources: chrisvoncsefalvay d3-patterns (re-authored as outlines). Vega-Lite gallery (used to confirm what is NOT native). D3 module docs (d3-sankey, d3-hierarchy, d3-chord, d3-force). Re-authored.
when_to_reach_for_d3: The intent maps to a type tagged vega_lite_native:false in chart_chooser.json (treemap, flow_map, hex/contour map, sankey, chord, network).

Vega-Lite genuinely cannot express the LAYOUT (a node-link layout, a hierarchical pack/partition, a flow ribbon). If Vega-Lite CAN do it, do it in Vega-Lite — do not drop to D3 for styling or familiarity.
An EXPLORABLE centerpiece that recomputes a custom layout live (component_implementations.json interactive_elements) — but reuse Vega-Lite + re-embed first if the chart type is native.

performance_rule.rule: SVG handles roughly <= ~2000 marks (nodes + links + cells) smoothly. Beyond that, interaction stutters — switch the rendering to CANVAS (or aggregate the data: bin, cap nodes, fold the long tail into 'other').
performance_rule.detail: Each SVG element is a DOM node; thousands of them make layout/repaint expensive, especially during d3-force ticks or zoom. Canvas draws to a single bitmap (no per-mark DOM). For a force graph, also stop the simulation after it settles (a tick cap or alphaMin) rather than running forever.
performance_rule.anti_pattern: A 10k-node force graph in SVG (jank, frozen tab); animating thousands of SVG nodes on every tick; never aggregating a dense flow.

sankey.intent: flow — volume between stages/categories; ribbon width = quantity
sankey.outline: Shape data as {nodes:[{name}], links:[{source,target,value}]}. Run the d3.sankey() layout (set nodeWidth, nodePadding, extent) over the graph -> it assigns x0/x1/y0/y1 to nodes and a width to links. Draw nodes as <rect>, links as <path d=sankeyLinkHorizontal()> with stroke-width = link.width, stroke-opacity low. Label nodes with the value.
sankey.editorial: Color links by source (or by a category); mute, accent the focal path. Cap nodes/links — aggregate the long tail into 'other' (a sankey with many thin ribbons is unreadable). Order nodes to minimize crossings.
sankey.perf: Usually well under the SVG ceiling; keep it that way by capping flows.

treemap.intent: part_to_whole — hierarchical, many items; nested rectangles by AREA
treemap.outline: Build d3.hierarchy(root).sum(d=>d.value).sort(...). Run d3.treemap().size([w,h]).padding(p) -> leaves get x0/y0/x1/y1. Draw a <rect> + clipped <text> per leaf. Optionally make it zoomable (click a node to re-layout its subtree).
treemap.editorial: Rectangle AREA encodes the value (area-not-radius spirit, encoding_craft.json) — area reads worse than length (channel hierarchy), so use treemap for 'show the whole composition with many parts at a glance', not precise comparison. Color by top-level category; label only rectangles big enough to fit text. Sequential shade for an ordered value (design_tokens.json).
treemap.perf: Hundreds of leaves are fine in SVG; thousands -> canvas or aggregate small leaves into 'other'.

chord.intent: flow — bidirectional flows among a fixed set of nodes around a circle
chord.outline: Input is a square matrix[i][j] = flow from i to j. d3.chord().padAngle(...)(matrix) -> groups (arcs around the ring) + chords (ribbons between them). Draw group arcs with d3.arc(), ribbons with d3.ribbon(). Color by source group; label arcs.
chord.editorial: Only for a SMALL fixed node set (~<12) — chord gets illegible fast. Mute, accent the focal relationships; dim others on hover. Sort groups meaningfully.
chord.perf: Bounded by node count squared (the matrix); keep nodes few.

sunburst.intent: part_to_whole — hierarchical composition as concentric rings (radial treemap)
sunburst.outline: d3.hierarchy(root).sum(...). d3.partition().size([2*PI, radius]) -> each node gets x0/x1 (angle) and y0/y1 (radius). Draw one <path d=d3.arc()> per node; inner ring = root's children, outer rings = descendants. Often made zoomable (click a wedge to re-root).
sunburst.editorial: Same caveat as treemap/pie — ANGLE+AREA read worse than length (channel hierarchy); use a sunburst when the HIERARCHY is the point, not for precise comparison. Color by branch; label only wide-enough wedges. Prefer a treemap or stacked bar if comparison matters more than hierarchy.
sunburst.perf: Hundreds of arcs fine; deep/wide trees -> canvas or collapse.

force_network.intent: flow/relationship — links among many entities; force-directed graph (incl. citation networks, component_implementations.json)
force_network.outline: Data = {nodes:[{id}], links:[{source,target}]}. d3.forceSimulation(nodes).force('link', forceLink(links).id(d=>d.id).distance(...)).force('charge', forceManyBody().strength(-)).force('center', forceCenter(w/2,h/2)). On each 'tick' update <line> (links) + <circle> (nodes) positions. Add d3.drag() to nodes and d3.zoom() to the <g>. Size nodes by a metric (AREA via scaleSqrt — encoding_craft.json); color by type (accent self / muted refs).
force_network.editorial: Stop the simulation once it settles (alphaMin or a tick cap) — don't run forever (perf + jitter). Tooltip on hover (title/year); click opens the link. Aggregate/cap nodes for big graphs.
force_network.perf: THE most likely type to blow the SVG ceiling. Beyond ~2000 nodes+links switch to canvas rendering and cap the simulation; consider pre-computing the layout for very large graphs.

flow_map_and_hexbin.intent: spatial — flows between places (flow map) or aggregated point density (hexbin/contour)
flow_map_and_hexbin.outline: Flow map: project origin/destination coords with a d3 projection; draw curved <path> per flow, width = volume, over a base geography (or a Leaflet base, component_implementations.json). Hexbin: bin projected points with d3.hexbin(), draw <path d=hexbin.hexagon()> per bin colored by count. Contour: d3.contourDensity() over points -> <path> bands.
flow_map_and_hexbin.editorial: These are the spatial types Vega-Lite/Leaflet can't natively express. For a simple choropleth or proportional-symbol map, DON'T come here — use Vega-Lite geoshape or Leaflet (chart_chooser.json spatial). Sequential scale from design_tokens.json; cap/aggregate flows.
flow_map_and_hexbin.perf: Hexbin/contour aggregate by design (good for dense data); many raw flow lines -> canvas.

do_not: Do NOT reach for D3 for any chart type Vega-Lite can express (bar/line/area/scatter/heatmap/boxplot/choropleth/etc.) — those are vega_recipes.json.
Do NOT exceed ~2000 SVG marks without switching to canvas or aggregating.
Do NOT skip the editorial rules (sort, area-not-radius, CVD-safe color, annotate the key datum) just because it's D3 — encoding_craft.json + annotation_layers.json still apply.
Do NOT add a charting framework — D3 from the allowed CDN only, inline, no build step.
